glossary_terms.definition: Central server process that runs projects, tag engine, and modules; the always-on core of an Ignition deployment.
Desktop authoring tool (JNLP/native launcher) for building projects, views, tags, and scripts.
Container for views, scripts, named queries, and resources deployed on a Gateway.
Modern browser-based, responsive HTML5 visualization module; primary UX in 8.3.
Legacy Java desktop client visualization module; mature but superseded by Perspective.
A Perspective screen/page unit composed of components; can be embedded and parameterized.
A UI building block (label, table, chart, container) with properties, events, and bindings.
Layout component (Flex, Column, Coordinate, Breakpoint, Tab) that positions child components.
Live link that drives a component/tag property from a tag, expression, query, or script.
Read-only formula language used in bindings and tags (math/string/date/logic functions).
Core data point (Memory, OPC, Expression, Query, Reference, Derived) in the tag engine.
Provider/folder path string identifying a tag, e.g. [default]Area/Motor/Speed.
Named namespace/scope hosting a set of tags on a Gateway.
Status flag (Good/Bad/Uncertain) indicating validity of a tag value.
Reusable, parameterized tag template enabling OOP-style tag design and inheritance.
Centrally managed, parameterized SQL query reusable across bindings and scripts.
Parameterized SQL that prevents injection and enables plan reuse.
Subsystem that logs tag values to a database for historical query and trending.
Buffering mechanism that queues history/data during DB outages and replays on recovery.
SQL Bridge feature mapping tags to DB rows on a schedule/trigger (standard/historical/block/stored-procedure).
Graphical step/transition logic engine for sequential process control.
Open industrial protocol for device data; Ignition acts as both client and server.
Module (Modbus, Allen-Bradley, Siemens S7, etc.) translating device protocols into OPC tags.
OPC-UA address-space identifier for an exposed data node.
Server-push mechanism delivering value changes at a sampling/deadband rate.
Minimum change threshold before a value update is reported, used to reduce load.
Execution context (Gateway/Vision/Perspective/Universal) that determines which functions are valid.
Built-in Python function library (system.tag, system.db, system.alarm, etc.).
Perspective mechanism for sending/receiving messages between sessions/components/gateway.
Script running in gateway scope on timer/tag-change/startup/shutdown events.
Non-blocking execution to keep the gateway/UI responsive during long operations.
Four-state model (Active/Cleared × Acked/Unacked) governing alarm lifecycle.
Historical log of alarm events queryable via components and system functions.
Multi-level notification pipeline that escalates unacknowledged alarms over time.
How users prove identity: Classic (internal), IdP (SAML/OIDC), LDAP/AD, OAuth2.
Authorization by roles/security levels applied to tags, views, and gateway config.
External SAML/OIDC service delegated for modern authentication.
Hierarchical authorization grant (advanced RBAC) checked on protected resources.
Pluggable .modl extension adding capabilities (Perspective, Reporting, MQTT, etc.).
Module providing Transaction Groups (tag↔DB row mapping).
Licensed module for designing/rendering data-driven PDF/other reports.
Cirrus Link module publishing tag data via MQTT/Sparkplug B for edge/IIoT.
Master/Backup gateway pair with state sync and automatic failover.
Activation role (not fixed identity) in a redundant pair; license follows role.
Automatic promotion of Backup to active on Master failure.
Failure mode where both nodes think they are active; avoided via tie-breaking.
DB-tier redundancy (master-slave/streaming/Always-On/Data Guard) behind gateways.
Reusable set of DB connections sized to avoid exhaustion under load.
Transaction concurrency setting controlling locking/consistency trade-offs.
DB engine's query strategy; read to diagnose slow queries.
Severity filter (TRACE→ERROR) for gateway/wrapper logs.
Gateway service log (wrapper.log) capturing startup/JVM/module output.
Responsive container switching layouts at a viewport width breakpoint.
Mobile delivery via progressive web app or thin native wrapper over a Gateway URL.
Reusable named style applied across components instead of inline styles.
Secure connection fabric linking multiple gateways for remote tags/services.
